description:
String of Pearls (Senecio rowleyanus) is a popular trailing succulent whose bead-like leaves make it visually appealing, but it is toxic to cats. The entire plant, including its sap, contains compounds that can cause internal and external irritation.

The plant is believed to contain pyrrolizidine alkaloids, which are known to be harmful to the liver, although the exact toxins have not been fully identified. Additionally, the plant's sap can irritate a cat's skin and eyes on contact. Because the round leaves are tempting for cats to bat at and chew, this plant poses a significant risk.

If a cat eats this plant, it may lead to vomiting, diarrhea, drooling, and noticeable tiredness or lethargy. Skin contact might cause redness or itching. Due to the risk of liver damage and other symptoms, place this plant completely out of your cat's reach. If you suspect your cat has eaten any part of it, contact your veterinarian.
name: String of Pearls
safetyNotes: Toxic compounds: pyrrolizidine alkaloids and irritant compounds throughout the plant; the round bead-like leaves may attract cats
Mechanism: PAs are metabolised to reactive pyrroles in the liver, causing hepatocellular necrosis; cumulative damage can lead to liver failure
Symptoms: vomiting, diarrhea, drooling, lethargy; chronic exposure may cause weight loss and jaundice as liver damage accumulates
The dangling bead-like appearance is particularly appealing to cats — relocate to spaces cats cannot access
Seek veterinary care if significant ingestion occurs

symptoms.name: Vomiting and diarrhea
symptoms.notes: If plant pieces are found in the cat's mouth, they should be removed and the mouth should be rinsed with water. Veterinary attention is recommended, especially if a large amount was eaten.

symptoms.name: Drooling
symptoms.notes: Drooling typically occurs as a direct response to oral irritation from chewing the plant parts or sap.

symptoms.name: Lethargy
symptoms.notes: Lethargy indicates a systemic reaction to the plant's toxins. If a cat becomes noticeably lethargic after eating the plant, the sources strongly advise contacting a veterinarian.

symptoms.name: Irritation of the skin and eyes
symptoms.notes: This localized irritation is specifically caused by direct physical contact with the plant's sap. Rinsing the cat's paws (and mouth) with water is recommended to remove the irritant sap.

treatments.description: Promptly and gently remove any remaining plant pieces from the cat's mouth.
treatments.name: Oral Decontamination (Removal of Plant Material)
treatments.notes: This is the most immediate step required to stop the cat from swallowing any more of the toxic leaves or sap.

treatments.description: Rinse the cat's mouth and paws thoroughly with water.
treatments.name: Topical and Oral Rinsing
treatments.notes: Because the sap from the String of Pearls is a known irritant to the skin and eyes, rinsing the paws is highly recommended to prevent the cat from rubbing the sap into its eyes or experiencing localized skin irritation.

treatments.description: Contact your veterinarian to inform them of the exposure and follow their guidance for further monitoring or supportive care.
treatments.name: Veterinary Consultation and Monitoring
treatments.notes: Seeking professional veterinary advice is especially critical if the cat ingested a large amount of the plant or if it is exhibiting lethargy.
